title: Physics National Model Exam 2 2024
description: Physics National Model Exam 2 2024 featuring 100 authentic questions with step-by-step solutions. Designed for Ethiopian national exam mastery.

questions.questionText: Electric field is defined as:
questions.explanation: E = F/q.

questions.questionText: Kirchhoff’s first law is based on:
questions.explanation: Sum of currents entering a junction equals sum leaving.

questions.questionText: Kirchhoff’s second law is based on:
questions.explanation: Sum of potential differences around a closed loop equals zero.

questions.questionText: A particle moves in a circle of radius 0.5 m with angular acceleration 4 rad/s². Find tangential acceleration after 3 s if initial angular velocity is 2 rad/s.
questions.explanation:
Tangential acceleration at = r * α = 0.5 * 4 = 2 m/s²;
 velocity after t = ω*t + 0.5*α*t² 
→ v_t = r*ω = 0.5*(2 + 4*3) =
 0.5*14 = 7 m/s, 
at = 6 m/s².

questions.questionText: Two discs, one solid and one hollow, same mass M and radius R, roll down same incline. Which reaches bottom first?
questions.explanation:
Moment of inertia I solid = 0.5 MR², hollow = MR² → a = g*sinθ/(1+k²/R²). 

Solid has smaller k²/R² → higher acceleration.

questions.questionText: A cylindrical tank with radius 1 m has hole at base. Water height = 4 m. Exit speed?
A sphere of mass 0.5 kg floats in liquid with 1/4 volume submerged. Find relative density of sphere.
questions.explanation:
ρ_sphere/ρ_liquid = submerged fraction 

→ ρ_sphere = 0.25 ρ_liquid.

questions.questionText: A wire of length 1 m moves perpendicular to 0.4 T field at 5 m/s. EMF induced?
Two resistors 8 Ω and 12 Ω in parallel. Equivalent resistance?
A particle in circular motion radius 0.6 m with speed 3 m/s. Centripetal acceleration?
Solid sphere mass 3 kg, radius 0.1 m rolls without slipping. Moment of inertia?
A sphere radius 0.05 m, mass 0.5 kg submerged 1/5 volume in liquid. Buoyant force?
Wire resistance 12 Ω carries 3 A. Potential difference across wire?
Capacitors 4 μF and 6 μF in series. Equivalent capacitance?
Satellite speed decreases with radius increase. Ratio of speeds if radius doubles?
questions.explanation: v ∝ 1/√r → if r doubles, v_new = v/√2.

questions.questionText: Battery 9 V, internal resistance 1 Ω, connected to 4 Ω resistor. Current?
Ball rolls off table 1 m high at 2 m/s. Horizontal distance?
Solid sphere rolls down incline. Mass = 2 kg, radius 0.1 m, v = 1 m/s. Rotational KE?
questions.explanation:
I = 2/5 mR² = 0.008, ω = v/R = 10 

→ KErot = 0.5*0.008*100 = 0.4 J (scaled to options).

questions.questionText: Charged particle moves perpendicular to uniform B. Radius formula?
questions.explanation:
Centripetal force from Lorentz:

 qvB = mv²/r → r = mv/qB.

questions.questionText: Planet in elliptical orbit. Where is speed minimum?
questions.explanation: Speed minimum at farthest point (aphelion) from star due to angular momentum conservation.

questions.questionText: Spring k = 200 N/m compressed 0.1 m. Energy stored?
Hollow cylinder rolls down incline. Acceleration compared to solid cylinder?
questions.explanation:
a = g*sinθ/(1+k²/R²).

 Hollow has larger k²/R² → smaller acceleration.

questions.questionText: Pipe carries fluid velocity 2 m/s wide section, 4 m/s narrow. Pressure difference?
Resistor 10 Ω, capacitor 2 μF in DC 12 V. Initial current?
questions.explanation: t=0 capacitor behaves as short → I = V/R = 12/10 = 1.2 A.

questions.questionText: A particle moves under a force F = (4i + 3j) N. Its mass is 2 kg. Find its acceleration vector.
A projectile is launched at 30 m/s at 45° to horizontal. Find its maximum height.
Two vectors A = 5i + 12j and B = -3i + 4j. Find magnitude of A-B.
A 2 kg block slides down 30° frictionless incline of 5 m. Speed at bottom?
Two point charges +3 μC and -2 μC separated by 0.5 m. Force on -2 μC?
questions.explanation:
F = k*q1*q2/r² =

 9e9*3e-6*2e-6/0.5² = 0.216 N attractive.

questions.questionText: A 6 μF capacitor charged to 12 V. Energy stored?
A radioactive substance has half-life 4 h. Fraction remaining after 12 h?
questions.explanation: n=12/4=3 half-lives → remaining=(1/2)^3=1/8.

questions.questionText: A resistor 8 Ω is connected to 24 V battery. Power dissipated?
A particle moves under a force F = (6i + 8j) N. Its mass is 2 kg. Find its acceleration vector.
A projectile is fired with 40 m/s at 60° to horizontal. Find its maximum height.
Two vectors A = 5i + 12j and B = -3i + 4j. Find magnitude of A-B.
A 3 kg block slides down a 30° frictionless incline of 5 m. Speed at bottom?
Heat required to raise 0.5 kg water from 20°C to 80°C (c=4186 J/kg°C)?
In nuclear physics, alpha decay emits:
questions.explanation: Alpha particle = helium nucleus (2p + 2n).

questions.questionText: Beta minus decay emits:
questions.explanation: A neutron transforms into a proton, emitting an electron and an antineutrino.

questions.questionText: Gamma decay emits:
questions.explanation: Gamma radiation is electromagnetic energy without charge or mass.

questions.questionText: Specific heat capacity is:
options: Heat required to raise 1 kg by 1°C
questions.explanation: It is an intrinsic property of material.

questions.questionText: Latent heat is:
options: Energy for phase change at constant temperature
questions.explanation: Latent heat does not change temperature but changes phase.

questions.questionText: Thermal conduction occurs due to:
questions.explanation: Vibrating atoms transfer energy via collisions.

questions.questionText: Equipotential surfaces have:
questions.explanation: All points on an equipotential surface have same potential.

questions.questionText: In rotational motion, angular momentum is conserved when:
questions.explanation: Angular momentum L = Iω remains constant if τ_ext = 0.

questions.questionText: Moment of inertia depends on:
questions.explanation: I = Σ m r² depends on how mass is distributed about rotation axis.

questions.questionText: Buoyant force equals:
questions.explanation: Archimedes’ principle.

questions.questionText: In 2D motion, horizontal velocity of projectile:
questions.explanation: No horizontal forces → horizontal velocity constant.

questions.questionText: In 2D motion, vertical velocity changes due to:
questions.explanation: Gravity accelerates projectile downward.

questions.questionText: Work done by centripetal force is:
questions.explanation: Force is perpendicular to displacement → W = F·d cosθ = 0.

questions.questionText: In a closed circuit, total current:
questions.explanation: Ohm’s law: I = V/R_total.

questions.questionText: Scalar product of two perpendicular vectors is:
questions.explanation: A·B = |A||B|cosθ, cos90°=0.

questions.questionText: Vector product of two parallel vectors is:
questions.explanation: A×B = |A||B|sinθ n, sin0°=0.

questions.questionText: Specific latent heat of fusion applies to:
questions.explanation: Fusion is phase change from solid to liquid.

questions.questionText: Specific latent heat of vaporization applies to:
questions.explanation: Vaporization is phase change from liquid to gas.

questions.questionText: In nuclear reaction, mass defect arises due to:
questions.explanation: Mass of nucleus < sum of nucleons → mass defect converts to binding energy.

questions.questionText: Coulomb’s law depends on:
questions.explanation: F = k q1 q2 / r².

questions.questionText: Electrons flow from:
questions.explanation: Electron flow is opposite to conventional current.

questions.questionText: Current is defined as:
questions.explanation: I = dq/dt.

questions.questionText: Potential difference across ideal conductor in equilibrium:
questions.explanation: No electric field inside ideal conductor → ΔV = 0.

questions.questionText: Rotational kinetic energy depends on:
options: Moment of inertia and angular velocity
questions.explanation: KE_rot = 0.5 I ω².

questions.questionText: In simple harmonic motion, acceleration is:
options: Proportional to displacement and opposite direction
questions.explanation: a = -ω²x.

questions.questionText: Voltage across series resistors:
questions.explanation: V = IR; current same → voltage proportional to resistance.

questions.questionText: In parallel resistors, voltage across each:
questions.explanation: All branches share same voltage in parallel.

questions.questionText: In fluid at rest, pressure at a point is:
questions.explanation: Pascal’s principle: pressure transmitted equally.

questions.questionText: Energy of alpha particle in decay comes from:
questions.explanation: Binding energy released converts into kinetic energy of alpha particle.

questions.questionText: Power in electrical circuit is:
questions.explanation: P = V*I.

questions.questionText: If the length and cross-sectional area of a wire are both doubled, the resistance will:
questions.explanation: R = ρL/A. If L becomes 2L and A becomes 2A, the '2's cancel out, leaving the resistance unchanged.

questions.questionText: The tangential velocity of an object in circular motion is doubled, and the radius is doubled. The centripetal acceleration:
questions.explanation: a = v²/r. New a' = (2v)² / (2r) = 4v² / 2r = 2(v²/r). The acceleration doubles.

questions.questionText: A calorimeter is typically made of copper because:
options: It has low specific heat and is a good conductor
questions.explanation: Copper's low specific heat ensures it absorbs very little heat itself, and its high conductivity ensures the contents reach thermal equilibrium quickly.

questions.questionText: Two charges attract each other with a force F. If one charge is tripled and the other is doubled, the new force is:
Which law of motion explains why passengers lean forward when a car suddenly stops?
questions.explanation: Inertia (Newton's First Law) states that an object in motion stays in motion. The passenger's body continues forward even though the car has stopped.

questions.questionText: What is the equivalent resistance of three 9Ω resistors connected in parallel?
questions.explanation: For identical resistors in parallel, Req = R/n. 9Ω / 3 = 3Ω.

questions.questionText: In projectile motion, the vertical component of velocity at the highest point is:
questions.explanation: At the peak, the object stops rising and is about to start falling, so its vertical velocity component is momentarily zero.

questions.questionText: A force 'F' acts on a mass 'm' for time 't'. The change in momentum is:
questions.explanation: Impulse (Change in Momentum) is defined as Force multiplied by the time interval over which it acts.

questions.questionText: What is the direction of current flow in a circuit according to 'conventional' current?
options: In the direction of electron flow
questions.explanation: Conventional current is defined as the flow of positive charge, which moves from the positive terminal to the negative terminal.

questions.questionText: A person runs 30m North and then 40m East. What is the magnitude of their displacement?
questions.explanation: Using the Pythagorean theorem for 2D motion: √(30² + 40²) = √(900 + 1600) = √2500 = 50m.

questions.questionText: The time required for half of the nuclei in a radioactive sample to decay is called:
questions.explanation: The half-life is a constant characteristic for a specific isotope, regardless of the initial amount.

questions.questionText: Newton's Third Law states that every action has an equal and opposite reaction. These two forces act on:
questions.explanation: Action-reaction pairs always act on two different bodies (e.g., foot kicks ball, ball kicks foot).

questions.questionText: Which of the following describes 'Latent Heat of Vaporization'?
options: Heat to boil liquid into gas without temperature change
questions.explanation: It is the energy required per unit mass to transform a substance from liquid to gas at its boiling point.

questions.questionText: An ideal voltmeter has ________ resistance.
questions.explanation: An ideal voltmeter should not draw any current from the circuit it is measuring, which requires an infinite internal resistance.

questions.questionText: A satellite in a circular orbit around Earth is in:
questions.explanation: Satellites are technically in a state of continuous free fall toward Earth, but their high tangential velocity causes them to miss the Earth and follow its curve.

questions.questionText: What is the result of 'Nuclear Fission'?
options: Splitting of a heavy nucleus into lighter ones
Loss of electrons from an atom
questions.explanation: Fission is the process used in nuclear power plants where a heavy nucleus like Uranium-235 splits into two smaller nuclei, releasing energy and neutrons.

questions.questionText: A 1kg mass is heated by 100J and its temperature rises by 2°C. What is its specific heat capacity?
Current is defined as the rate of flow of:
questions.explanation: Electric current (I) is the amount of charge (Q) passing through a point per unit of time (t).

questions.questionText: In 2D motion, if the velocity vector is perpendicular to the acceleration vector, the object is:
questions.explanation: When acceleration is perpendicular to velocity, it only changes the direction of the velocity, not its magnitude (speed), resulting in circular motion.

questions.questionText: Which type of radiation has the greatest penetrating power?
questions.explanation: Gamma rays are high-energy photons with no mass or charge, allowing them to pass through several centimeters of lead or meters of concrete.

questions.questionText: What is 'Thermal Conductivity'?
options: The ability of a material to store heat
The ability of a material to transfer heat
questions.explanation: Thermal conductivity (k) is a property that indicates how quickly heat can flow through a material via conduction.

questions.questionText: A force of 50N acts at an angle of 60° to the horizontal. What is the horizontal component of this force?
How do you increase the sensitivity of a potentiometer?
options: Decrease the length of the wire
Increase the length of the wire
questions.explanation: A longer wire decreases the potential gradient (V/L), meaning a larger change in length is required for a small change in voltage, making it more sensitive.

questions.questionText: The total energy of a nucleus is ________ the sum of the energies of its individual nucleons.
questions.explanation: Because of binding energy, the assembled nucleus is in a lower energy state than its free components.

questions.questionText: A ball is thrown upward. While it is rising, its velocity is ________ and its acceleration is ________.
questions.explanation: The ball moves up (velocity), but gravity pulls it down (acceleration), causing it to slow down.

questions.questionText: Which unit is used to measure the quantity of electric charge?
questions.explanation: The Coulomb (C) is the SI unit for electric charge.

questions.questionText: In a calorimetry experiment, why is the water stirred?
options: To ensure uniform temperature throughout the liquid
questions.explanation: Stirring ensures that the heat is distributed evenly so that the thermometer gives an accurate reading of the average temperature.

questions.questionText: What is the kinetic energy of a 2kg object moving at 3 m/s?
The resistance of an ideal ammeter is:
questions.explanation: To avoid changing the current it is trying to measure, an ammeter must have zero resistance.

questions.questionText: Which nuclear radiation is essentially a Helium nucleus?
questions.explanation: An alpha particle consists of two protons and two neutrons, which is identical to a Helium-4 nucleus.

questions.questionText: If the temperature of a gas is increased in a closed container, the pressure increases because:
options: Molecules collide with the walls more frequently and with more force
questions.explanation: Higher temperature means higher kinetic energy, leading to more frequent and more energetic collisions against the walls.

questions.questionText: A displacement-time graph with a curved line indicates:
questions.explanation:
A straight line on a d-t graph means constant velocity.

 A curve means the velocity is changing, which implies acceleration.

questions.questionText: Two resistors (R and 2R) are connected in series. The voltage across R is V. What is the voltage across 2R?
questions.explanation:
In series, V = IR. Since 'I' is the same for both, the voltage is proportional to resistance.

 2R will have twice the voltage of R.
